Today, on the call, we have with us Mr. Puneet Dalmia, Managing Director and CEO, Dalmia 
Bharat Limited; Mr. Yatin Malhotra, CFO, Dalmia Bharat Limited; and other senior 
management of the company. 
 
I would now like to hand the conference call over to Mr. Prassan Goyal, Head of Investor

Prassan Goyal: 
Thank you, Neerav. Good evening, everyone, and thank you for joining us today. I hope you 
had an opportunity to look at our financial results and presentation we have uploaded. Let me 
now hand over the call to Mr. Dalmia for his opening remarks. Thank you, and over to you, sir. 
Puneet Dalmia: 
Thank you, Prassan. It is good to be back with all of you as we discuss our Q2 results. I would 
begin by talking about the headlines shaping the world around us. The Russia-Ukraine war, the 
Gulf crisis, tariffs, financial and bond markets and El Niño, the world is going through multiple 
uncertainties. It seems that it has become the new normal, something we all have to live with 
day in and day out. 
 
I'm happy to see how India is navigating through these geopolitical challenges remarkably well 
with its fundamentals intact and strengthening. The country has demonstrated resilience in 
absorbing unprecedented external shocks while staying firmly on its growth path. The Q1 GDP 
was a case in point where the economy grew at 7.8%. Fiscal and policy measures, including 
sustained public spending and efforts to absorb the impact of rising fuel prices have helped 
cushion domestic economic activity and consumer sentiment from external shocks. 
 
We can see this reflected in a range of indicators. The RBI revised its financial year '27 GDP 
growth estimate upwards to 7.1%. GST collections remain close to record levels, while 
manufacturing output continues to show strong growth. Cement demand has also remained 
robust, growing in high single digit on a Y-o-Y basis during this quarter. This was supported by 
continued government capex spending, along with relatively low rainfall in several parts of the 
country.

In the first 5 months of the year, the central government has spent around 42% of its budgeted 
annual capex. The Ministries of Road Transport and Highways and Railways had also utilized 
around 45% of their respective annual budget outlays during this period, providing a meaningful 
impetus to cement demand. 
 
Having said that, rising inflation and potential onset of rate hike cycle pose near-term risks. But 
I believe India's growth story is much bigger than the near-term challenges we see today. The 
country is strengthening, growing and aspiring. Just like India, we at Dalmia are also building a 
stronger and sustainable organization for the future. And despite near-term challenges, we 
remain firmly focused on executing our strategic priorities across the board. 
 
I'm happy to mention that we have recently lit our new clinker line at Belgaum and commenced 
trial runs ahead of schedule. This additional capacity will help us deepen our presence in our 
stronghold markets of Karnataka and Maharashtra. As I couldn't think of a better time to bring 
this capacity online, we look to commence commercial production ahead of the peak demand 
season in Q4. Our expectations at Pune and Kadapa are also progressing as planned and are 
expected to come during financial year '28, taking our total capacity to around 67 million tons. 
The Central India story is another exciting one, which is unfolding. 
 
Based on our initial integration experience, the assets are in good shape, and our teams are 
working relentlessly to restart operations and ramp up production as quickly as possible. At 
Rewa, we have restarted mining operations while both the clinker line and the cement mill are 
steadily ramping up under trial runs. 
 
While Q2 saw some initial teething issues as we continue to build on network and stabilize plant 
operations, I'm confident that we are on track to achieve a 35% to 40% utilization of these assets 
by end of financial year '27. Another area I would like to touch upon is our sales strategy. While 
East and Northeast markets remained subdued during the quarter due to severe floods and heavy 
rainfall, we saw healthy momentum in both South and West markets with growth approaching 
double digits. Our focus on strengthening our brand position remains equally strong. 
 
Premium product share continues to increase, and we expect this trend to deepen over coming 
quarters as we continue to drive this initiative of premiumization. Our recently launched 
premium offering, Weather365, has received an exceptional response from the market, 
prompting us to accelerate its rollout into newer markets. Let me briefly touch upon the current 
operating scenario. Elevated crude oil prices and rising input costs have been testing the 
resilience of the entire industry. With crude prices remaining above $100 a barrel and maritime 
disruptions continuing, international petcoke prices has surged to about over $180 per ton. 
 
Against this backdrop, I believe we have managed the impact reasonably well through fuel mix 
optimization, better planning and several other initiatives. In the first half of the year, we have 
seen war-related impact of around INR220 per ton on variable cost with additional pressures 
from key input materials such as packing bags, adding another INR100 per ton. 

 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
Dalmia Bharat Limited.

While pricing in Q1 helped us absorb some of these cost pressures, the environment was 
relatively challenging in Q2 in a few key markets. Prices remained steady in South and West, 
while East pricing was under pressure amid subdued demand. That said, we are now beginning 
to see a more encouraging price trend. Both September and October have seen healthy price 
increases, helping us recover a part of the cost inflation. 
 
We are hopeful that the positive momentum will continue going forward. While these industry 
cycles may come and go, our long-term strategic priority remain firmly anchored, maximizing 
returns from existing assets, expanding in a calibrated manner to become a pan-India player 
while maintaining a strong and healthy balance sheet. And underpinning all of this is our 
continued investment in our people, processes and organizational culture. 
 
As we continue to march forward to chase our vision, one of my key priorities is to build a 
future-ready organization with strong leadership team and deep capabilities. In that spirit, in a 
planned transition, effective 1st January 2027, Navin Tewari, our Chief Marketing Officer, will 
transition as a key adviser to me on strategic initiatives and projects. 
 
Over the past year, he has helped deepen our engagement with channel partners, sharpen our 
market positioning and strengthened our sales capabilities, thereby strengthening the foundation 
for the company. As a part of this transition, Yatin Malhotra, our CFO, will take additional 
responsibility for sales and marketing, along with his existing responsibility for the finance 
function. 
 
Yatin joined Dalmia Bharat Group in March last year and has led various enterprise-level 
initiatives since then. I'm confident that his familiarity with Dalmia way of working and his C-
level experience over the last 11 years across various consumer-facing organizations provide the 
right combination of business strategy and financial management. 
 
I wish him well as he takes on this additional responsibility. Our focus remains clear: strengthen 
our brand positioning, deepen our market reach and further build our sales capabilities to 
generate strong returns for our shareholders and support the next phase of growth. I'm confident 
that these changes will bode well for us as we look forward. 
 
Thank you, and over to you, Yatin, for the financial updates. 
Yatin Malhotra: 
Thank you, Puneet ji, and good evening, everyone. Building on to Puneet-ji's comments, India 
witnessed healthy demand trends during the quarter, supported by strong public spending and 
resilient consumption. Below normal rainfall in several parts of the country also allowed 
construction activity to continue for longer, providing further support to cement demand. We 
benefited from these trends in our South and West markets. On the other hand, East and 
Northeast were considerably weaker, impacted by heavy rainfall. 
 
Having said that, we are now seeing demand picking up well across these regions also. In line 
with the regional trends, our volumes grew 4% Y-o-Y during the quarter on an ex-Central basis. 
Overall volumes rose 3% to 7.1 million tons in the quarter.

I would also like to highlight the progress we are making in strengthening Dalmia's brand in the 
market. We have deepened our engagement with channel partners and refreshed how our brand 
shows up in the marketplace with a new look across our hoardings, packing bags and other brand 
touch points. 
 
As part of this journey, we have also taken another important step. Konark, which has been a 
cornerstone of our portfolio and a trusted brand for decades, is now getting phased out as we 
sharpen our focus on premiumization. This marks an important milestone towards reinforcing 
our brand positioning and building a stronger, more unified Dalmia brand. 
 
Let me now turn to our quarterly performance. Since our Central India operations are still at a 
nascent stage, I will take you through our performance, excluding the Central markets. Prices 
remained largely stable across regions, unlike the usual moderation that we see in quarter 2.  
However, East witnessed some price corrections amid subdued demand, reflected in roughly 1% 
Q-o-Q decline in our realizations. Incentives during the quarter declined to INR25 crores with 
relatively lower production at plants where incentive accrued. 
 
However, we expect this to normalize as demand picks up. Collections during the quarter 
remained healthy at INR53 crores. We are already seeing cement prices inching up steadily with 
prices in the South and East currently around INR15 per bag higher than Q2 average. This should 
provide some support in offsetting the rising cost pressures. 
 
Moving to costs. Our total cost in the quarter increased by roughly INR260 a ton on an ex-
Central basis. Let me take you through the key factors driving this increase. Variable costs 
increased by around INR200 per ton. Higher fuel costs alone contributed around INR100 per 
ton, while inflation in key raw materials added another INR30 to INR40. 
 
During the quarter, we also saw a meaningful change in the regional mix with lower volumes in 
East, resulting in an additional adverse impact of INR50 to INR60 per ton. With external cost 
pressures persisting and petcoke prices remaining above $180 per ton, we expect a further cost 
impact of around INR75 per ton in quarter 3.  
However, at the same time, the adverse mix impact seen in quarter 2 should get reversed as the 
regional mix normalizes. I would also like to highlight one additional point. As you are aware, 
following the recent amendments to the MMDR Act, the mineral bearing land tax is no longer 
applicable with effect from August 22. 
 
These payments have been discontinued in Assam and Meghalaya from that date, while they 
continue to apply in Tamil Nadu. We are engaging with the relevant authorities to facilitate this 
discontinuation. Until then, the impact of this tax continues to be reflected in our raw material 
cost. 
 
Separately, the amendment to the MMDR Act has also resulted in a significant reduction in the 
contingent liabilities by roughly INR198 crores, and the liabilities now stand at INR931 crores.

Consequently, contingent liabilities as a percentage of the net worth have declined to almost 5%, 
which is among the lowest in the industry. This reflects our continued focus on strengthening 
governance and proactively managing potential liabilities.  
Renewable energy remains an important pillar of our cost efficiency initiatives, and we are 
making strong progress on this front. Over the last 5 years, we have scaled our RE capacity from 
63 megawatts to roughly 450 megawatts today, significantly increasing the RE share to 52% in 
quarter 2. 
 
Going forward, we will continue to accelerate this transition with more RE capacity getting 
online over the next few quarters. In line with this transition, we have impaired around 97 
megawatts of thermal power capacity this quarter, where operations have been discontinued. 
This has been done in 3 of our existing plants, which do not include the central plant.  
Logistics is another area where we continue to innovate and find efficiencies. Despite the impact 
from diesel price increase of about INR20 per ton in this quarter, our cement freight cost has 
remained largely flat. Clinker freight has also declined, led by efficiencies and regional mix 
change. 
 
Coming to fixed costs, comprising of employee costs and other expenses, the increase was about 
INR168 per ton. Of this, approximately INR140 per ton was attributable to under absorption of 
fixed costs due to Q-o-Q decline in volumes, while the remaining increase was largely driven 
by higher shutdown costs during the quarter. As volumes recover, under absorption should 
normalize over the coming quarters.  
Putting it all together, the decline in realization by about INR49 per ton, combined with cost 
increases of approximately INR259 per ton on an ex-Central basis, resulted in an EBITDA per 
ton declining to INR746. On a reported basis, EBITDA per ton stood at INR698, reflecting a 
dilution of roughly INR50 per ton due to Central plants. 
 
We expect this dilution to increase to about INR100 to INR125 per ton in quarter 3 as Rewa 
commences commercial production before it progressively reduces as Central operations scale 
up. During the quarter, we reported exceptional items aggregating INR339 crores.  
I've already spoken about the transition from the Konark brand and the impairment of captive 
power plants. In addition to this, we have implemented a separation scheme for eligible 
employees at a few units, resulting in a one-time provisional charge of INR57 crores. 
 
Briefly touching upon our ongoing projects. We are making good progress on our expansion 
plans. The trial run at Belgaum's clinker line were initiated ahead of schedule. 3 MTPA cement 
mill is also expected to go in trial in the next couple of weeks. Both Pune and Kadapa are also 
progressing as planned.

INR1,420 crores. Capex guidance for the full year remains unchanged at INR3,200 crores to

one of our foremost priorities. Guided by this, we remain committed to maintaining leverage 
below 2x on a sustainable basis, which will create a strong financial foundation for the Dalmia's 
next phase of growth.
